page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel x86_64 CPU containing 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The system features 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core, alongside a 16 MB L3 cache. For acceleration, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation and 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average tier across multiple categories. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68 and a multi-core score of 14175.12. Memory performance shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 784.94 GB/sec, dropping to 88.57 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with large block write bandwidth at 52.63 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 27.58 GB/sec, while bzip3 decompression achieved 10.45 GB/sec single-threaded and 40.69 GB/sec multi-threaded. The shared CPU allocation represents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained, highly intensive CPU-only workloads.

This server offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card. This resource density makes it highly suitable for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not saturate a full A40, such as moderate machine learning inference, data science jobs, and CUDA-based development. The combination of 40.0 GB RAM, a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and a Redis SET throughput of 14.91 million operations per second also makes it a strong candidate for database hosting, caching layers, and web serving applications.
